title: Synology patches critical DSM OAuth flaw (CVSS 9.8) and NGINX HTTP/2 flaw (CVSS 8.1)
date_note: Date the Synology advisories SA_26_21 and SA_26_20 were published.
summary: Synology published two advisories on 19 November. CVE-2026-120382 (CVSS 9.8) lets remote attackers read or write arbitrary files or conduct denial-of-service attacks through the DSM OAuth API. CVE-2026-123007 (CVSS 8.1) is an NGINX HTTP/2 heap buffer overflow. The revised advisories list fixes in DSM 7.4.1-90080-2 and 7.3.2-86009-6, with other versions marked OnGoing. Neither mentions exploitation.
plain: Synology has warned of two serious flaws in the software of its NAS storage devices. Fixed versions exist for DSM 7.3 and 7.4; fixes for other versions are still ongoing, and the vendor gives workarounds.
exec: Synology rates the DSM OAuth flaw Critical (CVSS 9.8) and says remote attackers can read or write arbitrary files; fixes exist for DSM 7.3 and 7.4.
action: Synology advises upgrading to DSM 7.4.1-90080-2 or 7.3.2-86009-6 or above. For versions it lists as OnGoing, Synology's workarounds are to deactivate the OAuth Service package and disable HTTP/2 under Control Panel > Network > Connectivity.
impact: DSM 7.1 to 7.4 and BeeStation OS 1.5 are listed as affected; DSM 7.2.x, 7.1 and BeeStation OS had no fix yet when read (advisories marked Ongoing).

validation.note: Synology's own advisories SA_26_21 and SA_26_20 (primary, read in full) and GBHackers, which independently reports the same CVEs and scores. Neither states exploitation.
